subject: SSO / KMS retention exception — triage & mutual action plan
messages:
From: Susan Perez <susan@harborhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Audit evidence request + temporary BYO retention exception

Hi Jordan —

We got an audit notice that requires our vendors to provide 90-day SSO session logs and key custody evidence for the period of May–Jul 2027. Our security team (audit@harborhealth.com) is asking whether Redwood can: 1) provide exported session logs for SSO events (login, token refresh, logout) for the requested window, and 2) allow a temporary BYOK retention carveout so we can retain a wrapped copy of our CMK for 120 days in escrow for the auditor.

Can you confirm whether these are possible and what the formal steps are? We’ll need a small mutually agreed action plan and dates because the audit deadline is Aug 20. I attached the audit scope.

Thanks —
Susan Perez
Director IT Risk, HarborHealth
Attachments: Harbor_health_audit_scope.pdf (application/pdf, 312KB)

Hi Susan —

Thanks for sending the scope. Looping in Security (Grace) and Product (Marissa) to triage. High-level: we generally provide SSO session logs and can produce scoped exports; BYOK/escrow requests need an exception path and legal sign-off.

Grace / Marissa — can you confirm a practical workback and the minimum artifacts (export format, hashing of wrapped CMK, audit-friendly statements) we can deliver by Aug 20? If we’re doing a temporary escrow, what is our recommended retention window, and what operational steps do we need (storage, access controls, attestation)?

I'll draft a short MAP once we align on owners.

- Jordan
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit evidence request + temporary BYO retention exception

Jordan / Marissa —

Reviewed the scope. Quick points from Security ops:

- SSO session logs: we can export login/token-refresh/logout events from the identity audit index. Exports are CSV/JSON with timestamps and user_id hashes. We'll need HarborHealth to confirm the principal identifiers they want (email vs. user_id).

- BYOK escrow: Redwood can support an "escrow" procedure for a wrapped CMK stored in an encrypted bucket for a time-limited window, but this is an exception to our standard retention policy. Requirements: signed exception request, legal approval, a defined TTL, and a read-only audit workflow for access. We also recommend keeping a hash of the wrapped key (SHA256) in the ticket for integrity checks.

- Proposed temporary window: 120 days maximum from the date of deposit. We can do 120 days but suggest 60 days if Harbor prefers shorter. We need an owner in Harbor for the deposit and a one-person access recovery SOP (2FA + operations approval).

- Evidence artifacts: exported logs, KMS escrow receipt (hash + metadata), attestation email from our SOC engineer. Ops runbook excerpt attached.

Action items (security):
1) Generate a scoped SSO export (format: newline-delimited JSON).
2) Prepare an escrow receipt template and compute wrapped-key hash.
3) Provide a short attestation statement for auditors.

I can own (1) and (2) if Marissa confirms product gating for the UI/controls, and Jordan coordinates the signed exception.

Grace O'Connor
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: ops-runbook-excerpt.pdf (application/pdf, 88KB)

Thanks — some product constraints and proposals from my side:

- UI / Policy: We don't currently have a first-class console flow for creating a temporary escrow retention exception that shows TTL to the customer. Any escrow will be an ops-handled process for now (manual).

- Export tooling: We can produce exports via the admin exports endpoint (rate-limited); for near-term, we should run a one-off export job and deliver the files to a secure share. Long-term, we should track this as a self-serve feature (RED-3982).

- Security considerations: We need legal-approved wording in the exception request describing liability and destruction obligations. Also confirm whether Harbor wants the wrapped key copy stored encrypted under Redwood's envelope key or if Harbor will provide an encrypted blob directly. The latter reduces our surface area.

- Timeline: If Security (Grace) can provide the export by Aug 10 and escrow steps by Aug 12, I can prepare a small UI/ops checklist and escalate any product engineering needs post-audit. For now, this is an "ops + legal" exception path, not a product change.

Proposed owners: Jordan (Harbor contact + exception request), Grace (exports + escrow receipt), Marissa (product checklist & post-audit roadmap).

Marissa Cole
Director, Product Management — Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Jordan
